nodes.name: Haryana Entrepreneur & Startup Policy
nodes.description: The Haryana Entrepreneur & Startup Policy provides a Seed Grant of up to INR 3 Lakhs per startup for idea validation, prototype development, and other related activities.

eligibility: A startup must be incorporated in India as a private limited company, partnership firm, or limited liability partnership.
A startup must not have been incorporated more than seven years ago, except for biotechnology companies, which can be up to ten years old.
A startup must have an annual turnover not exceeding INR 25 crore in any preceding financial year.

A startup must be working towards innovation, development, or improvement of products, processes, or services, or have a scalable business model with high potential for employment generation or wealth creation.
A startup must not be formed by splitting up, reconstruction, demerger, or reconstitution of an existing business.
A startup must not be a holding company or a subsidiary of any firm already in existence, except the subsidiary of another startup.

sources.evidence: Reimbursement of 25% of lease rental subsidy to eligible startup units established in the state, operating from Incubators/IT Parks/Industrial Clusters or any other notified location shall be eligible for a period of 1 year subject to the ceiling of INR 1lakh per annum.

Cost reimbursement for max 3 Patent/Quality certification per Unit up to a limit of INR 2 lakh for domestic & INR 5 lakh for International Patent/Quality certification upon successfully receiving them.

Government will empanel software/mobile app development agencies for extending programming/app development support to eligible startups, and would reimburse development cost to the tune of 60% for application development undertaken through empaneled agencies, to the ceiling of INR 1 lakh per startup.

A Seed Grant up to INR 3 Lakhs per start-up shall be provided for validation of idea, prototype development, assistance towards travelling costs and carrying out field/ market research/ skill training/marketing and initial activities to setup a startup etc.

Startup means an entity (Private, Public, Proprietary, Partnership Firm), incorporated in India: As a private limited company (as defined in the Companies Act, 2013) or registered as a Partnership firm (registered under Section 59 of the Partnership Act, 1932) or a limited liability partnership (under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008) in India;
Not prior to seven years and in the case of Biotechnology Companies this period shall be up to 10 years;
With annual turnover not exceeding INR 25 crore in any preceding financial year;
Working towards innovation, development or improvement of products or processes or services, or if it is a scalable business model with a high potential of employment generation or wealth creation

Provided that such entity is not formed by splitting up, or reconstruction, of a business already in existence and should not have been formed by the demerger or reconstitution of a business already in existence;
Provided that such entity is not a holding company and it is not a subsidiary of any firm already in existence or except the subsidiary of any startup;
Location: The company/entity be registered in Haryana under the Haryana Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 1958 ;
Employment: The company employs at least 50 (fifty) per cent of its total qualified workforce in Haryana, which shall not include contract employees.

nodes.name: Mitacs Globalink Research Internship
nodes.description: A research internship program for third-year undergraduate students in AICTE-approved institutions to undertake a 12-week research project in Canada.

eligibility: The applicant must be a 3rd-year full-time student of an undergraduate program (B.E / B.Tech) in an AICTE-approved institution in the year of application.
The applicant must have a minimum CGPA / GPA of 85% in the 2nd year.
The applicant must be at least 18 years of age.
The applicant must be able to spend twelve (12) weeks between May and September at a university in Canada on a research project related to their area of interest and expertise.
The applicant must be able to demonstrate oral and written fluency in English or French, depending on the primary language of the project as indicated by the Canadian host professor.

nodes.name: Startup Funding Support
nodes.description: This service provides funding support to startups in the form of Seed Support and Sustenance allowance.

metadata.fee: There is no application fee for the scheme.

sources.evidence: There is no application fee for this scheme.
Eligible Startup may get registered on the online portal (www.startup.gujarat.gov.in) to avail assistance under the scheme.
The Start-ups will apply to Nodal Institution with requisites (Application form, Supporting Documents and Undertaking) in prescribed format.

Nodal Institution will have to examine the case of Startups thoroughly from the viewpoint of evaluation parameters. After exercising due diligence, Nodal Institution will take decision and recommend (in prescribed format) the startup project proposal to the office of the Industries Commissioner within 15 working days from the submission of application.

In case of unwillingness of Nodal Institution to incubate Startup, Nodal Institution shall communicate to the Startup about decision of their proposal with valid reasons within 15 days from the submission of application.

The Startup Gujarat Cell will scrutinize each application against the basic eligibility criteria and verify the submission of all required documents from the checklist. Complete proposals received from Nodal Institutions will be forwarded to iCreate, while incomplete proposals will be returned to the Nodal Institutions within 15 working days.
iCreate will conduct a detailed evaluation through an Expert screening committee, comprised of domain experts, and submit their recommendations to the Startup Gujarat Cell within 20 working days.
After exercising due diligence, the Startup applications will be placed before the State Level Empowered Committee (SLEC) within 30 days from the recommendation of Expert Screening Committee.
State Level Empowered Committee (SLEC) shall meet once a month preferably for approve (eligible assistance), reject or recall Startup project proposal.
Startup Gujarat Cell will communicate the decision of SLEC to the Nodal Institutions within 10 working days.
Accordingly, Nodal Institution will communicate the decision of SLEC to the respective Startups on the same day.
Note: In essence, Eligible Startups gets approval for Seed Support and Sustenance allowance within 90 working days from the submission of their application at Nodal Institution.

nodes.name: Rajasthan Startup Policy
nodes.description: The Rajasthan Startup Policy provides financial assistance and support to innovators and startups at various stages, including sustenance allowances, marketing assistance, capital grants, and support for incubators and entrepreneurship cells.

sources.evidence: Rs. 10,000/- per month will be provided to the innovator as sustenance allowance for one year.Startups whose project is recommended by the Nodal institution and approved by the Committee will get a sustenance allowance of Rs. 10,000 per month for a period of 1 year.
Marketing/Commercialization assistance upto a maximum of Rs. 10 lakh shall be provided to Startups to launch its products/services in the market.

A one time grant for capital items will be given to Host Institutes by the State Government for the purpose of entrepreneurship development and startup events in the region, with a maximum of Rs. 50 lakh.

A grant of maximum 25% of the investment to be given to established and reputed Corporates, VCs and Angel Investors by the State Government for the creation of fixed assets to set up new incubation centres, with a maxium limit of Rs. 50 lakh. This grant is subject to a maxium of 5 per year and 2 per district.
A matching grant of upto Rs. 10 lakh will be given to competent institutions and individuals like Incubators, angel investors etc. to run Accelerator Programmes in Rajasthan.
The colleges will be given a one-time grant of Rs. 10 lakh to establish and operate an E-Cell.
